clue.text: Stalk two hundred gathered round a German car by the French

indicators.note: to gather round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, twice over

explanation.surface: A trader with two hundred cars stalks round a German motor parked by a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: Two hundred splits into its two Cs, which sit either side of the car. The answer is one word despite the printed (4,4).
explanation.definitionFit: A caudicle is the slender stalk linking the pollen mass of an orchid to its sticky gland, a botanical term.

clue.text: Joint sometimes having an international following

definitions.text: Joint sometimes having an international following

parts.words: Joint sometimes having an international following
parts.note: surface reading: a pub or club that draws fans from abroad
setter's reading: an international player is a cap, and this body joint is sometimes followed by the word cap

explanation.surface: A bar or nightspot that attracts a crowd from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A player picked for his country wins a cap; put cap after this joint and you get the bone at the front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the leg hinge between thigh and shin, and the bone shielding it is called the kneecap.

clue.text: Medical drink exercises one Spanish saint

parts.note: the Spanish title for a saint, as in San Francisco

explanation.surface: A tonic that a Spanish holy man prescribes along with workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A ptisan, usually spelt tisane, is an infusion of barley or herbs taken as a remedy for the sick.

parts.note: ex- marks what something once was, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A statement that there used to be plenty of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is an instance or illustration of something, which is what an example gives.

clue.text: Plume (first class) grew mainly on dry point

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the last letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: A1 means first class, written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A first-rate feather that sprouted on a dry headland.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a classic shorthand for first-rate, and its 1 is read as the letter I. TT means teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is a tuft of feathers, originally egret plumes, worn as an ornament on a hat or headdress.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal 'really, no kidding'
second meaning: frank and upright in dealings

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase of emphasis; the words are two separate meanings of the same expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase is used as an adverb meaning really and as an adjective for someone frank and sincere.

clue.text: Appendage allowed to be worn on the limb

indicators.note: in a down entry, something worn on top sits above, so the second piece is placed first

explanation.surface: An extra part permitted to be strapped to an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn round the upper arm, an accessory attached to the body as an added piece.

parts.note: gains are increases or steps forward
a duty is a levy, a tax

explanation.surface: A fee that pushes a customs levy up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gains tax is a levy on profits from selling assets, so it is a charge imposed by government.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to confine, especially in wartime
second meaning: a junior hospital doctor in the US

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to detain a US doctor; the verb and noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to detain someone such as an enemy alien; in the US the noun names a newly qualified physician in training.

clue.text: This time zone's ends get the chopper

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters of zone

explanation.surface: In this era and region, the axe falls.
explanation.walkthrough: AD, Anno Domini, labels years of the present era.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool like an axe with its blade set crosswise, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: Exercise high season flavouring, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

explanation.surface: Holiday-time seasoning, according to the gossips.
explanation.definitionFit: A somersault is a gymnastic move of rolling head over heels, a physical exercise.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the working mechanism of a watch

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a spell of sentry duty during a war; the watch is a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch's action is its internal movement, and soldiers who see action are engaged in fighting.

parts.note: surface reading: a sociable man who finds friends easily
setter's reading: he causes other people to become acquainted with each other

explanation.surface: A description of a friendly, outgoing chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presents one person to another creates a new acquaintance between them, which is what this person does.

parts.note: to touch off a fuse is to light it
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Sue set off a single gap, as if lighting a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb meaning take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to bring a lawsuit, to go to court against someone.

clue.text: Revolutionary month opening with very large note

parts.note: a vent is an outlet or aperture

explanation.surface: A rebellious month kicks off with an enormous banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize. Revolutionary refers to the French Revolution's calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventose, the windy month, was the sixth month of the French Republican calendar, roughly February to March.

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means sitting above it, so the first piece goes first

parts.note: short for specification, a set standard
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Bogus rules piled on top of what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means plausible on the surface but actually wrong, so misleading and untrue.

indicators.note: manoeuvres are moves and repositionings, so the letters of the preceding word are shifted about

explanation.surface: A commendation of men who took part in military exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation is a reference to or naming of something, and to mention is to refer to it briefly.

clue.text: Exaggerate the speed of a game of cricket?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: value something more highly than it deserves

definitions.text: the speed of a game of cricket
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, the number of overs bowled per hour

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; the over rate measures how fast a side gets through them.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to praise beyond merit, an overstatement of worth; split, it names a cricket pace statistic.

clue.text: Characteristics of a German city church

definitions.note: plural in the clue, the answer is singular

parts.note: an industrial city in the Ruhr

explanation.surface: The features of a church in a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic nature of something, the qualities that make it what it is.

definitions.note: a collective noun; the answer is a plural noun
an adjective; the answer is a plural noun for mistakes

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a woman named Flora is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora looks like a woman's name; it is plant life. Bloomers is also British slang for gaffes, besides being old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that blossom are bloomers, and in British slang a bloomer is an embarrassing mistake.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a prison or jail cell
second meaning: a lockable garage or storage unit

explanation.walkthrough: Cooler suggests a fridge, which would also store things, but it is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockup is a jail where prisoners are held, and also a rented garage or unit kept secured for storage.

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A small tipple bought for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is informal British slang for a small child or boy.

explanation.surface: A ruler left behind a single orange essence.
explanation.definitionFit: Neroli is an essential oil distilled from the blossom of the bitter orange tree, used in perfume.

clue.text: He scans, namely, routine retinue without turn, perhaps

indicators.note: a routine is a set sequence of moves, suggesting the letters are put through a new order

parts.note: R for a right turn, set on the outside

explanation.surface: An official reads through a list of an entourage's routine moves.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, scilicet, is the dictionary abbreviation for namely. The parse is loose: the extra R has to come from turn, read as right, with without meaning outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer examines things closely, especially ballot papers at an election count, so he scans them.

parts.note: the word that pairs with neither

explanation.surface: A girl has a partner of neither sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Nora is a girl's name, a short form of Eleanor or Honora.

parts.note: surface reading: something we are rightly owed
setter's reading: what we are entitled, that is called or titled

explanation.surface: A claim to something that is ours by right.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle once meant to give a title to, so what we are each entitled is what people call us.

clue.text: Say, d'you know the state capital

indicators.note: to say a phrase is to speak it, so its spoken form gives the answer

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking whether you know the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Juneau is the capital city of Alaska, one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: She is previously synonymous with Tarzan's lady

definitions.text: She is previously synonymous with Tarzan's lady

parts.words: She is previously synonymous with Tarzan's lady
parts.note: surface reading: a woman who used to be identified with Tarzan's partner
setter's reading: the word placed before Jane, Tarzan's mate, to name a Wild West heroine

explanation.surface: A woman who was once taken for Jane of the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan's lady is Jane; the word to put in front of Jane gives Martha Jane Canary's nickname, the frontierswoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamity Jane was a famous American frontierswoman, so the first word of her nickname is what she was called.
